text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementEnvironmentPlants Experience Optical Illusions, TooYou don’t need a brain to get fooledJCBy Jake Currie5:30 PM CST on November 3, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleOptical illusions can be a little frustrating. You know that the two lines are the same length, or the image isn’t moving, etc., but you can’t force your brain to process the information that way, no matter how hard you try. Per a new study published in Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, even organisms with no brains, like plants, can get fooled by optical illusions. Powered By 10 ShareNextStayAccording to a team of botanists from Tel Aviv University who uncovered this odd phenomenon, the secret is in the way the plants receive information from light. Your light receptors are located on the front of your face, but plants have light receptors all over their bodies (and primarily on their stems).
